Calculation of Modularity for a List of igraph Objects

Source: R/modularity.R
calc_modularity.Rd

This function calculates the modularity of a list of networks provided in the ig parameter. Modularity measures the strength of division of a network into modules (communities).

Usage

calc_modularity(
  ig,
  ncores = 0,
  cluster_function = cluster_spinglass,
  directed = FALSE
)

Arguments

ig

A list of igraph objects for which modularity will be calculated.

ncores

Number of cores used for parallel computation. If set to 0, sequential processing is used.

cluster_function

The igraph clustering function to use, or a function that returns an igraph communities object (e.g. run_infomap()). Default cluster_spinglass.

directed

Logical; if TRUE and the network is directed, the directed modularity of the partition is computed. Default FALSE (undirected modularity), which is consistent with the default cluster_spinglass() because it ignores the direction of the edges. Use TRUE only with a clustering function that takes the direction into account, e.g. run_infomap(directed = TRUE).

Value

A data frame with a column Modularity containing the modularity values for each network.

Details

Note: cluster_spinglass() only works on networks with a single connected component.

The modularity is always recomputed from the membership of the partition with igraph::modularity(), and not taken from the value stored in the object returned by the clustering function, because that value is not comparable between algorithms (for cluster_spinglass() it is not the weighted modularity of the partition). If a network has a 'weight' edge attribute it is used both by the clustering function and to compute the (weighted) modularity.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
nullg <- generateERbasal(netData[[1]], 10)
calc_modularity(nullg)

# Directed modularity with an algorithm that uses the direction of the edges
calc_modularity(netData[[1]], cluster_function = run_infomap, directed = TRUE)
} # }
